segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello. Welcome to Real Easy English. In this podcast we have real conversations in easy English to help you learn. I'm Neil.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And I'm Georgie. Visit our website to find all the vocabulary from this episode and a free transcript.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hi Georgie. How are you doing this week? Are you feeling healthy?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Today I'm feeling healthy. I had a healthy lunch but this weekend I ate a lot of chocolate.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And this week we're talking about our healthy or not so healthy habits.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK, well let's get started.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Neil, what do you do to stay healthy?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, I try to eat well. So that means not eating too much and not eating too much fat or salt or sugar.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But that's what I try to do, not always what I do.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: It really difficult for me especially It difficult not to eat too much sugar I love a sweet treat

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: have you got a sweet tooth

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I do have a sweet tooth So maybe we should explain a sweet treat which is anything that is sugary like a pastry or a donut or something chocolate And a

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: sweet tooth, Neil? What's a sweet tooth?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, if someone has a sweet tooth, it means they like

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: sweet things, like you.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes, I have a sweet tooth, definitely.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So Georgie, you like sweet things,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: but what do you do to be healthy?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: OK, yes, I do eat a lot of sweet treats

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: but to stay healthy I am very good at walking to places.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So instead of taking public transport or driving,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I like walking and that's...

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I think that's good for you, isn't it?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, walking's good or riding a bike.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I'm not very good at riding a bike.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: It's too scary in London.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: It feels too dangerous.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: What do you think you could be better at when it comes to your health?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes, well, as we know, I eat a lot of chocolate,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: so I could be better at having a healthy diet,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: eating less chocolate and eating more vegetables.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: What about you, Neil?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: What could you be better at?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I think I could probably get more sleep actually Sleep is very important for your health and I never seem to sleep enough

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: No, you're always tired. You're always complaining about not sleeping enough.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So, Georgie, are you going to change your health habits soon?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: OK, yes, I will. I'll change my habits soon. Let's start next week.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Next week. Why not tomorrow?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: because I don't want to.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Give me a bit more time.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: When are you going to change your habits?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Soon?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, I would like to sleep for many months,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: but it's not going to happen.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I will still be waking up too early, I'm sure.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But maybe I should drink less coffee,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: go to bed earlier and spend less time on a screen.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yeah, that sounds like a good plan.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So, Georgie, we know all the advice for staying healthy.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Do you find it hard, though, to stay healthy?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes, I do find it difficult because we know the advice,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: we shouldn't eat too much sugar, but I still want my sweet treat

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: at the end of the day. It makes me happy.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well if it makes you happy it probably healthy

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yeah OK let look again at some of the language we heard during the conversation We had healthy

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: diet food that is good for you.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Advice opinions about what you should do. For example, to stay healthy, you should ride

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: a bike to work.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: We heard soon used to describe something that will happen in a short amount of time.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: For example, I'm going on holiday soon, next week.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And still, used to describe something that is continuing.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: For example, you still like chocolate, even though it's unhealthy.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: We learned sweet treat, something sugary that you enjoy.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And we heard sweet tooth. If you have a sweet tooth, you like sweet food.
